Article Title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia exit may cost him around Rs 900 crore: How much wealth does he have left?
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang

Where does Huang's $144.5 billion fortune come from?

Huang has already pocketed $3 billion

Evolution of Nvidia

Can Huang turn his shares into cash

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia founder Jensen Huang’s exit from the chipmaking giant may cost him almost $108 million in stock awards, according to Bloomberg.While the amount, over Rs 900 crore in INR terms, sounds huge, it is only a tiny fraction of the massive fortune he has built over 33 years at the company. With an estimated net worth of $144.5 billion, the Nvidia co-founder is set to give up just 0.07% of his wealth following his exit.Also Read| Nvidia in Chaos: Trump unlikely to raise Alice Huang allegations with Xi Jinping during China meeting Huang’s departure comes at a time when Nvidia shares have taken a hit.The company’s market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025 following news of his resignation. However, despite the fall, Huang’s biggest source of wealth remains his existing shareholding, valued at around $135 billion.The $108 million he is set to lose comes from stock awards that have not yet vested. Under Nvidia’s equity compensation policy, executives forfeit their unvested restricted stock units (RSUs) when they leave the company.Huang held around 346,000 such units and was expected to receive about 310,000 shares under the company’s equity incentive plan, provided certain performance targets were met.Following his exit, he will forfeit these unvested awards.Jensen Huang has already slipped out of the top 10 of Forbes' richest people list, with his wealth declining by $2.8 billion, or 1.97%. According to Nvidia's annual report and proxy statement for fiscal year 2026, Huang received total compensation of $36,343,830 during the year, down from $49.87 million in the previous financial year.His compensation package included a base salary of around $1.5 million, stock awards worth approximately $24.8 million and $6 million in non-equity incentive plan compensation. The remaining amount was classified as other compensation.Almost all of Huang's wealth is tied to Nvidia shares. Unlike several other technology leaders, he has built his fortune mainly through owning the company's stock rather than stock options or other executive benefits.He owns around 812 million Nvidia shares, worth approximately $135 billion at Thursday's closing price. This makes him the company's largest individual shareholder. His holding represents less than 5% of Nvidia, while his voting stake stands at around 3.5%.According to Bloomberg's wealth index, Nvidia shares account for nearly 97% of his total fortune.His holdings are spread across shares owned directly by him, family trusts and holding companies. His charitable foundation separately holds around 59 million Nvidia shares, valued at more than $9 billion at current prices.Despite his substantial holding, Huang does not have special voting rights because Nvidia has only one class of shares.His salary and other cash payments form only a small part of his wealth. He received around $7.5 million in cash compensation in each of the past two years.Also Read| Nvidia spy scandal: What Jensen Huang told top executives about his relationship with Alice Huang Although Huang has held on to most of his Nvidia shares, he has sold around $3 billion worth of stock since the company went public in 1999, according to Capital IQ data and company filings.For most of his time as chief executive, his annual share sales remained relatively small, rarely crossing a few hundred million dollars. That changed as Nvidia's valuation climbed during the AI boom.Huang sold around $713 million worth of shares in 2024, followed by approximately $1 billion in 2025. These sales were made through pre-arranged trading plans as Nvidia's market value crossed $3 trillion and later $5 trillion.He has not sold any shares so far this year, according to the data.With Huang no longer leading Nvidia, attention is also turning to whether he will begin selling more of his shares. However, offloading such a large holding may not be easy.His share transactions could be affected by potential lengthy legal investigations into his relationship with a Chinese executive at a major Nvidia customer. Analysts at William Blair have described the matter as a “significant overhang on Nvidia shares in the near term”.There are also restrictions on when he can trade because of information he may have received while heading the company.Jesse Fried, a corporate governance expert at Harvard, said Huang would have to wait until material negative information that could affect Nvidia's share price became public before selling.“Huang can start selling as soon as any negative material non-public information he learned while CEO is disclosed,” Fried said.He is “OK to sell knowing undisclosed positive information, because [he] can’t profit from that,” Fried said.Nvidia's results next Tuesday could clear the way for Huang to start selling, provided he does not hold any other insider information, lawyers said.The size of his holding is another challenge. His 812 million shares are equivalent to around six days of Nvidia's total trading volume. Selling a large number of shares at once could put pressure on the stock price, meaning any sale would probably have to be spread over several months.Huang has also avoided borrowing against his Nvidia shares. Unlike some other technology billionaires, he has not pledged his stock as collateral for loans, as Nvidia does not allow its executives to do so.
Article Summary: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia may cost him almost $108 million in stock awards. With an estimated net worth of $144.5 billion, the Nvidia co-founder is set to give up just 0.07% of his wealth following his exit. Huang’s departure comes at a time when Nvidia shares have taken a hit.

Article Title: As gold falls from Rs 1.8 lakh peak to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, Indians buy 30% more, spending Rs 72,000 crore on 52 tonnes; silver demand rises 10%
Article Text:
In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%.

Gold price correction from Rs 1.8 lakh peak

Gold generates big returns

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gold prices falling from their record highs has led to Indian consumers increasing their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year, according to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA). Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.The industry body estimated that consumers purchased 52 tonnes of gold worth Rs 72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at Rs 5,400 crore during this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali celebrations.The increase followed a correction in gold prices from a peak of around Rs 1.8 lakh to Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams, drawing buyers back into the market. Purchases made in advance of the wedding season, which starts in mid-November and runs until March, also helped boost demand.“Jewellers have made good business in this year’s Dhanteras and Diwali,” IBJA national secretary Surendra Mehta told ET.Mehta said the market was witnessing pent-up demand, as several consumers had put off buying gold after Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to people not to purchase the metal.“Consumers had stayed away from the precious metal. But since the price has fallen and there is a chance of prices moving northwards again as Brent crude prices have fallen, people have come out to buy gold. In fact, buying is still continuing .”The festival calendar also worked in favour of jewellery purchases. Dhanteras was observed on November 6, followed by Diwali on November 8. Both occasions fell in the early part of the month, when salaried employees typically receive their monthly pay and festive bonuses.“This has resulted in healthy cash flow in the market, encouraging consumers to shop enthusiastically. Gold prices have also been relatively lower over the past four to six months, further improving purchasing sentiment,” said Rajesh Rokde, chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council.In the current fiscal year through September, gold sales by volume declined by nearly 50%. The fall was attributed to higher prices, an increase in import duty and Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s appeal to consumers to refrain from buying gold.Despite the volatility, gold has generated significant returns over the past few years. Prices, which were around Rs 60,000 per 10 grams in 2023, climbed to Rs 80,000 in 2024 and reached Rs 1.15 lakh-Rs 1.20 lakh in 2025. During this year’s Dhanteras-Diwali period, prices stood at approximately Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams. Silver has also recorded a substantial appreciation in value.An analysis of eight years of business performance by Bengaluru-based C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers found that gold sales volumes during this festive season were the third-highest in a decade, even though prices were around 10% above their level a year earlier.“The overall sentiment has remained unshaken, with consumers continuing to repose confidence in gold jewellery despite the unprecedented rise in prices over a 12-month period,” said C Vinod Hayagriv, director of C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers.Natural diamonds also held up well, registering their second-highest sales volume in eight years. The retailer recorded a 250% increase in natural diamond sales on Dhanteras, while sales during the Diwali season rose 47%.The performance comes at a time when the natural diamond industry is facing disruption from global sanctions affecting Russian diamond supplies and increasing competition from lab-grown alternatives. However, lab-grown diamonds are emerging as an additional product category rather than displacing natural diamonds.
Article Summary: Indian consumers increased their purchases of precious metals during the Dhanteras-Diwali period. Gold demand rose 30% in volume terms and silver buying grew 10% compared with the corresponding period last year. Jewellers said the trend pointed to a recovery in demand ahead of the important wedding season.

Article Title: Nvidia loses $500 billion since last week amid 'spy' scandal; Jensen Huang slips to 13th on Forbes rich list
Article Text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday after reports came out on multiple affairs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang, extending a weeks-long selloff in the chipmaker amid concerns over the company's leadership and the future of the artificial intelligence boom. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19.The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Its shares are now around 30 per cent below the record high touched on October 6, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market capitalisation over the past month. Nvidia's market value slipped below $4 trillion, a level it had not breached since July 2025, reported Reuters. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.The selloff marks a sharp reversal for a company that became the world's most valuable publicly listed business on the back of the global AI boom. Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), which power artificial intelligence systems and data centres, made it a central player in the technology industry and one of Wall Street's biggest market drivers.Its shares had surged more than 1,700% over four years before the recent correction, while its market capitalisation had briefly crossed $5 trillion.Huang's departure has also taken a toll on his personal fortune. The Nvidia co-founder, who had been among the world's 10 richest people, has seen his wealth fall sharply alongside the company's stock. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires rankings, he slipped two places from eighth to tenth earlier this week. His estimated fortune subsequently fell further, pushing him out of the top 10 to 13th position.Also read: Trump unsure woman linked to Jensen Huang was a spy; report alleges 3rd affair of ex-Nvidia CEO The fallout extended beyond Nvidia to companies closely linked to its AI ecosystem. Nvidia-backed cloud computing firm CoreWeave fell 8.1 per cent, while Nebius plunged 18 per cent after cutting its 2026 revenue forecast amid delays in adding third-party capacity. Super Micro Computer also dropped 12%. However, rival chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom gained more than 4 per cent each, as investors assessed whether Nvidia's leadership turmoil could create opportunities for competitors.Nvidia is also due to report its quarterly results next week, with investors watching its revenue growth and outlook.The turbulence in Nvidia also played out against a volatile session on Wall Street, although the broader market managed to recover most of its early losses. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,592.40, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 189.40 points, or 0.4%, to 52,297.09. The Nasdaq Composite also shed 0.4% to close at 25,366.09, after falling as much as 1.6% earlier in the session. Rising oil prices following US President Donald Trump's remarks on Iran added to market pressure, with Brent crude climbing 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel.
Article Summary: N Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19. The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.

Article Title: Mother Dairy, Amul milk gets costlier: Dairy giant hikes rate by upto Rs 6 per litre from Thursday; check prices
Article Text:
Mother Dairy raises prices

Why are milk prices increasing?

How much will milk cost now?

Full cream milk (packaged): Rs 76 per litre, up from Rs 72.

Rs 76 per litre, up from Rs 72. Toned milk (bulk vended): Rs 60 per litre, up from Rs 58.

Rs 60 per litre, up from Rs 58. Toned milk (packaged): Rs 62 per litre, up from Rs 60.

Rs 62 per litre, up from Rs 60. Double-toned milk: Rs 56 per litre, up from Rs 54.

Rs 56 per litre, up from Rs 54. Cow milk: Rs 65 per litre, up from Rs 62.

Rs 65 per litre, up from Rs 62. Full cream buffalo milk: Rs 86 per litre, up from Rs 80.

Nandini had also raised milk prices in Karnataka

NEW DELHI: Milk is set to get costlier in Delhi NCR from November 12, with dairy companies Mother Dairy and Amul increasing prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre. The price hike comes amid lower milk supplies and higher costs of buying milk from farmers.The increase will vary across milk varieties. Toned milk will cost Rs 2 more per litre, full cream milk Rs 4 more and full cream buffalo milk Rs 6 more, according to industry sources.In Delhi-NCR, full cream packaged milk will now cost Rs 76 per litre, compared with Rs 72 earlier. Packaged toned milk will cost Rs 62, up from Rs 60, while toned milk sold through bulk vending machines will cost Rs 60 against Rs 58 earlier.Double-toned milk will become costlier from Rs 54 to Rs 56 per litre. Cow milk prices will rise from Rs 62 to Rs 65, while full cream buffalo milk, which contains 6.5% fat, will cost Rs 86 against Rs 80 earlier.Mother Dairy, the largest milk supplier in Delhi-NCR, had last increased prices on May 14, 2026.Milk procurement has become more expensive for dairy companies. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months, while higher cattle feed prices have added to farmers' costs.Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production and availability usually improve. The shortage has affected the availability of milk fat, making it more expensive for dairy companies.When fresh milk supplies fall short, companies usually use milk powder and milk fat to prepare liquid milk. However, higher milk fat prices have also increased the cost of this process.Dairy companies have raised the prices they pay farmers to encourage them to produce and supply more milk. Amul has increased the procurement rate linked to milk fat to Rs 1,000 per kilogram. This allows farmers to receive more than Rs 60 per litre for milk, according to industry sources.Mother Dairy has decided to pass on part of these higher costs to consumers. The company pays farmers 75-80% of the money it earns from milk sales, sources told PTI.Here are the revised prices of different milk varieties in Delhi-NCR:Mother Dairy sells around 35 lakh litres of milk every day in Delhi-NCR through its outlets, general trade and e-commerce platforms. Its total daily milk sales across markets exceed 50 lakh litres.The company reported a 17% rise in turnover to Rs 20,300 crore in the last fiscal year. The growth was driven by higher demand for its milk products and cooking oils.Started in 1974, Mother Dairy is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB). It sells milk and milk products under the Mother Dairy brand, edible oils under Dhara, and fresh fruits and vegetables, frozen vegetables, snacks, pulps and concentrates under Safal.Before the latest increase by Mother Dairy and Amul, Nandini had raised milk prices in Karnataka. The state Cabinet approved an Rs 8 per litre increase in the base price, with the new rates taking effect from November 1.The Karnataka government said the increase was needed to protect dairy farmers facing severe drought conditions. Law and parliamentary affairs minister Krishna Byre Gowda said the revised prices were still within the range charged in most other states.He also said rising prices of other goods had hurt farmers and milk supply in Karnataka had fallen by 10 lakh litres due to the drought this year.Cooperation minister Laxman Savadi said the government also had to consider the possibility of farmers selling their milk to other states if prices were not increased. This could have led to a shortage of milk in Karnataka.Under the revised arrangement, Rs 7 of the Rs 8 per litre increase was to go to farmers, while Re 1 was allocated to milk unions in the state.
Article Summary: Mother Dairy and Amul increase prices by Rs 2 to Rs 6 per litre. Milk fat prices have risen by around 20-25% over the past few months, while higher cattle feed prices have added to farmers' costs. Milk supplies have also tightened despite the flush season, when production and availability usually improve.

Article Title: US flight disruption: Air India flags possible delays to US operations
Article Text:
Air India warns of disruptions to flights to and from America

Network router problem suspected

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Air India flights operating to and from the US could face disruptions after a communication outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to impose a nationwide ground stop on departures.The airline said the disruption had affected departures from airports across the country, potentially impacting its US operations. It has advised passengers to check their flight status before setting out for the airport and plan their travel accordingly."A nationwide ground stop is currently in effect across the US due to communication outages affecting air traffic operations. As a result, departures from airports across US are impacted, with possible consequential disruptions to Air India flights to and from the US," the airline wrote on X.Air India said its teams were monitoring the situation closely and would provide further updates as they became available.However, the ground stop has now been lifted according to Reuters, but the disruption is likely to continue.The chaos follows the FAA's had halted departures across the country on Friday after a telecommunications outage affected regional air traffic control operations. The restriction brought departures to a standstill at airports across the US, leaving thousands of passengers facing disrupted travel plans.The FAA said the decision was taken "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety".The outage affected all 22 regional air route traffic control centres, which direct aircraft travelling between airports. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said FAA technicians were investigating the problem, while the agency maintained that the communication disruption made it unsafe for flights to continue departing normally.Also Read| US flight chaos: Nearly 500 departures disrupted, thousands stranded as FAA halts take-offs nationwide; what we know so far The precise cause of the outage remained under investigation. However, according to an airline source cited by CNN, the FAA informed carriers that a problem with network routers had triggered the disruption. The issue was believed to have started at Chicago Midway International Airport before spreading across the country.During initial crisis discussions, the FAA was reportedly unable to give a clear explanation of the problem. Different facilities were experiencing the outage in different ways.Homeland security secretary Markwayne Mullin said the problem appeared to be related to telecommunications. Officials had no indication that it was the result of an attack, although authorities were examining the communication systems used by air traffic controllers.Also Read| Trump rules out cyberattack, AI as US probes nationwide flight disruption The ground stop prevented aircraft from taking off, but flights that were already airborne were allowed to continue to their destinations and land. Officials said they were assessing aircraft still in the air on a case-by-case basis.The nationwide suspension was the first since January 2023, when a malfunction in a key FAA computer system disrupted flight operations. It was also only the second such order since the September 11, 2001, attacks.
Article Summary: Air India flights operating to and from the US could face disruptions after a communication outage forced the FAA to impose a nationwide ground stop on departures. The FAA said the decision was taken "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety" The ground stop has now been lifted according to Reuters, but the disruption is likely to continue.

Article Title: TRAI's spam crackdown: Regularity authority bars 1.24 lakh telecom resources, blacklists 374 entities over violations
Article Text:
Representative image

TRAI receives 15.29 lakh spam complaints

Promotional and service calls assigned separate number series

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Over 22 crore consumers registered on DND registry

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) barred more than 1.24 lakh telecom resources from outgoing services and blacklisted 374 entities for one year for violating unsolicited commercial communication (UCC) rules during July-September, as the regulator intensified action against spam calls and messages.According to TRAI's quarterly report for the second quarter of 2026-27, 1,10,325 telecom resources, including mobile numbers, were barred from outgoing services for 15 days for a first violation. Another 13,777 resources were disconnected for one year after repeat violations.The regulator also blocked 3,725 SMS headers and blacklisted 374 senders for a year. During this period, the blacklisted entities cannot obtain fresh telecom resources.TRAI received 15.29 lakh complaints about unsolicited commercial communications during the quarter, of which 7.23 lakh were classified as actionable.The complaints came against the backdrop of 714.01 billion calls and 702.28 billion SMSes originating from telecom networks across the country. The complaint rate stood at around 2.14 per million outgoing calls, the report said.The TRAI DND App remained the main channel for reporting spam, accounting for 14.21 lakh complaints, or 92.9% of the total.The application had recorded 42.36 lakh downloads by September 30.Telecom operators' artificial intelligence-based systems flagged 19.9 billion incoming calls and SMSes as suspected spam during the quarter. These included 18.28 billion calls and 1.62 billion SMSes.Operators also issued more than 45.9 lakh warning notifications to entities suspected of sending spam communications. They carried out electronic know-your-customer (e-KYC) verification of 34,025 suspected senders, while 9,977 were disconnected for failing the KYC verification process.TRAI has introduced dedicated numbering series to help consumers distinguish promotional calls from service and transactional communications.Promotional calls are routed through the 140 series, while the 1600 series is meant for service and transactional calls from entities in banking, financial services and insurance, as well as government-to-citizen communications.A separate 1601 series was introduced on August 10 for service and transactional calls from utilities, logistics and delivery companies.During the quarter, 15.27 billion promotional calls originated through the 140 series. Of these, 1.70 billion were blocked after verification against registered Do Not Disturb preferences.Registered telemarketers also originated 660.71 billion commercial SMSes, while 11.09 billion promotional messages were blocked following preference verification.The report showed that 22.449 crore consumers had registered their communication preferences on the DND registry as of September 30. This represented 16.64% of the country's 134.9-crore subscriber base.More than 112 crore subscribers had not registered any preferences and remained accessible to commercial communications from registered senders and telemarketers.TRAI said its consumer awareness initiatives during the quarter included campaigns across radio, television, newspapers and social media. It also conducted 322 physical consumer awareness programmes, involving around 31,000 participants.In addition, more than 3 billion SMSes were sent to consumers to promote the DND App.The regulator said its quarterly enforcement data was compiled on the basis of information furnished by telecom service providers.
Article Summary: TRAI received 15.29 lakh complaints about unsolicited commercial communications during the quarter, of which 7.23 lakh were classified as actionable. Complaints came against the backdrop of 714.01 billion calls and 702.28 billion SMSes originating from telecom networks.

Article Title: Dollar nears 19-month high as inflation fuels bets on bigger Fed rate hike next month
Article Text:
US dollar set for biggest weekly gains

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The US dollar was heading for its biggest weekly gain in two months on Friday, staying close to a 19-month high as traders increased their bets on a larger interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve next month. The yen, meanwhile, remained close to the 160-per-dollar mark, keeping the possibility of Japanese government intervention in focus.Stronger-than-expected US inflation data this week and comments from Federal Reserve officials have led traders to expect a bigger-than-usual rate hike next month.This has also pushed up US treasury yields. Two-year Treasury yields have risen around 32 basis points this week to nearly 4.84%, putting them on track for their biggest weekly rise since April 2025.According to the CME FedWatch tool, traders are pricing in a roughly 92% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike next month."The dollar is still firm and that's driven by a robust jobs report and an acceleration of the CPI," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex. "We've had a series of hawkish comments from Fed officials this week including from (New York Fed President John) Williams and (Fed Governor Christopher) Waller."The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of currencies, rose 0.1% to 103.34. It remained close to its highest level since April 2025 and was heading for its biggest weekly rise since September. This would be its third consecutive week of gains.The euro fell 0.23% to $1.103 after touching its lowest level against the dollar since April 2025. It was also set for a fourth straight week of losses.The dollar gained 0.28% against the Swiss franc to 0.837, putting it on track to end two consecutive weeks of losses.Meanwhile, Japanese yen remained weak at 159.84 per dollar on Friday, close to its lowest level since early September. It has fallen around 1% this week and is heading for its biggest weekly decline since September.The yen's fall has raised concerns about possible intervention by Japanese authorities. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Friday that the government would respond appropriately to currency volatility.Elsewhere, the Australian dollar fell 0.46% to $0.678. It has been the worst-performing G10 currency against the dollar so far this month. Australia is also the only G10 country where markets expect an interest rate cut next year.The New Zealand dollar slipped 0.29% against the greenback to $0.553 and was heading for its third consecutive week of losses.Cryptocurrencies also recorded losses. Bitcoin fell 4.73% to $68,126.21, while ethereum declined 5.02% to $1,914.61.
Article Summary: The US dollar was heading for its biggest weekly gain in two months on Friday. The yen, meanwhile, remained close to the 160-per-dollar mark, keeping the possibility of Japanese government intervention in focus. Stronger-than-expected US inflation data this week and comments from Federal Reserve officials have led traders to expect a bigger rate hike next month.

Article Title: Binance restores withdrawals across 87 networks after record $6.3 billion crypto theft
Article Text:
Binance targets full reopening of withdrawals by next week

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Binance is working towards restoring withdrawal services across all its remaining networks and assets by the end of next week, following a security breach that led to $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency being stolen from the exchange last month.The company said it had brought 87 networks back online this week as part of its phased efforts to resume withdrawals. It had begun reopening the service earlier this month after covering 95% of the tokens lost in the attack."This week, we reopened withdrawals for 87 networks. We will aim to reopen withdrawals for all remaining networks and assets by the end of next week," Binance said in a post on X on Saturday.The October 29 theft has been described by experts as the biggest cryptocurrency heist ever. Binance's first account of the incident outlined a hacking operation involving several stages, which reportedly started in June before a series of security breaches led to the eventual theft.Responsibility for the attack has been a point of contention. Both the FBI and Binance have identified North Korea as being behind the breach, while Pyongyang has denied the allegations. Blockchain investigation firms have linked the incident to a North Korean hacking group called "TraderTraitor".The scale of the stolen assets has also drawn attention to the security risks surrounding digital currencies and the potential consequences for Binance. The exchange has committed to reimbursing customers in full.The incident was followed by a change in the company's senior finance team. Kaiser Ng, who had spent more than five years as Binance's finance chief, stepped down just over a week after the theft to pursue a new venture.Justin Yek, who took over the role, is a longtime finance executive and previously served as vice-president of finance at Airwallex.
Article Summary: Binance is working towards restoring withdrawal services across all its remaining networks and assets by the end of next week. The company said it had brought 87 networks back online this week as part of its phased efforts to resume withdrawals. It had begun reopening the service earlier this month after covering 95% of the tokens lost in the attack.

Article Title: Wall Street's next big bet: S&P 500 set to climb 14% despite slowing earnings growth - report
Article Text:
Wall Street outlook

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Wall Street's recent losses may not spell trouble for long, with Goldman Sachs seeing room for a fresh rally in the coming months. The brokerage expects the benchmark S&P 500 to reach 8,700 points over the next 12 months, as lower stock valuations could help markets gain ground despite a slowdown in corporate earnings growth.The target implies an upside of more than 14% from the index's last closing level of 7,592.40 points. According to Goldman Sachs, the recent market correction has made stocks more attractively valued, creating room for equities to deliver positive returns.The forecast follows a sharp selloff in shares of some of the biggest technology companies. The decline came after the Democratic victory in last week's US midterm elections fuelled concerns about a possible slowdown in data centre expansion.Goldman Sachs, however, expects the market to keep moving higher despite the possibility of slower growth. The brokerage estimates that earnings growth across global markets could at least halve in 2027. In the US, the pace could drop to 11% from 36%, possibly as hyperscalers ease the pace of their capital expenditure growth.This could put pressure on earnings across the AI infrastructure sector, where spending has been a key factor.But Goldman Sachs believes lower valuations, continued economic and earnings growth, softer bond yields and easing inflation could help equities stay in positive territory next year.The S&P 500 is currently trading at around 18.5 times its 12-month forward earnings, considerably lower than its recent highs of more than 23 times, the brokerage said.Goldman Sachs has retained its 'overweight' rating on US and Japanese equities, indicating a preference for these markets. It has maintained a 'neutral' stance on Asia and emerging markets, while keeping Europe at 'underweight'."From here, we expect equities to generate positive returns, albeit with higher volatility than in recent years," Goldman Sachs said.Meanwhile, the AI trade has faced another round of uncertainty amid developments at chipmaker Nvidia. The company's long-time CEO Jensen Huang quit following reports of alleged extramarital affairs, adding to concerns surrounding the AI sector.Nvidia's valuation has also fallen sharply. The stock is trading at around 11.7 times its 12-month forward earnings estimates, its lowest level since February 2012, according to data compiled by LSEG.
Article Summary: Goldman Sachs expects the benchmark S&P 500 to reach 8,700 points over the next 12 months. The target implies an upside of more than 14% from the index's last closing level of 7,592.40 points. According to Goldman Sachs, the recent market correction has made stocks more attractively valued, creating room for equities to deliver positive returns.

Article Title: US assures India of tariff advantage over rival economies under proposed trade pact
Article Text:
Tariff advantage promised to India, services issues pushed to second tranche

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The United States has assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over competing economies under the proposed bilateral trade pact, news agency PTI quoted a senior government official as saying, even as negotiations on the initial tranche and the broader agreement continue."The US has assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over its competitors in the trade deal. We will have to see how the tariff framework unfolds," the official said.However, the official cautioned that the extent of the advantage would depend on the final tariff structure. The outcome of the second investigation initiated by the office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) against India is also awaited.India is aiming to conclude the first tranche of the trade deal by the end of the current financial year, the official said. Negotiations are progressing simultaneously on the initial tranche and the broader Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA).Services-related issues will not be included in the initial package and will instead be taken up during discussions on the second tranche, which will form part of the larger BTA, the official added.The official said the final agreement would take the form of a legal text accompanied by annexures, with a dedicated chapter on customs and trade facilitation.Earlier, another senior commerce ministry official told ANI that India and the US had held discussions on customs and trade facilitation last week. A two-member US team had visited India on November 2-3 for talks on the issue, the official said.The two countries have been negotiating the trade pact in phases, seeking to secure early gains through the first tranche while continuing discussions on more complex issues under the broader agreement.
Article Summary: The US has assured India of a comparative tariff advantage over competing economies under the proposed bilateral trade pact. The extent of the advantage would depend on the final tariff structure. The outcome of the second investigation initiated by the office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) against India is also awaited.

Reservation Against Cancellation or RAC is an often talked about class of tickets that allows you an assured berth on a train, but on a sharing basis. Now, Indian Railways is examining whether it should discontinue the RAC facility. According to this TOI report , the proposal is being considered amid concerns about passenger comfort and whether a reservation arrangement that has existed for decades needs to be reconsidered.“There is a view that when a passenger isn’t getting full sleeping space, it may not be appropriate to charge the full fare,” said an official.Let’s first understand what is Reservation Against Cancellation ticket:RAC is a train ticket under which two passengers share a single berth even though each is charged the full fare and receives only half the sleeping space.RAC originated at a time when railway reservations were largely processed manually and there was no electronic mechanism to track cancellations and vacant berths in real time.Under the system, two passengers could be accommodated on one berth, with the possibility of one of them being allotted a full berth if the other passenger cancelled the ticket.RAC bookings can also lead to uncomfortable situations when a male and a female passenger are allotted the same seat.Ticket examiners often find it difficult to arrange alternative accommodation in such cases.Basically RAC allows passengers to travel in a reserved coach with confirmed sitting accommodation. However, Indian Railways' reservation rules do not guarantee them a full berth for sleeping.RAC passengers may be allotted full berths that become available because of cancellations or passengers not turning up before the train departs.When cancellations create vacancies, these berths can be allotted to RAC passengers before waitlisted travellers are given confirmed accommodation.Berths that fall vacant during the journey may also be assigned to RAC passengers under the applicable railway rules. If no full berth is available, passengers must continue their journey using the reserved sitting accommodation that is allotted to them.RAC status does not guarantee every passenger a separate sleeping berth. Nor does it mean that all RAC passengers must necessarily share a side-lower berth in every situation.The accommodation provided depends on the reservation and berth-allotment arrangements applicable to the particular train and class of travel.The rules governing cancellations and refunds are determined by the applicable railway refund provisions. The amount refunded and the charges deducted depend, among other factors, on the status of the ticket when the cancellation is made.The key distinction is that RAC permits passengers to travel with reserved sitting accommodation, while a full berth is allotted only if one becomes available.RAC tickets can be cancelled or refund applied online up to half an hour before the scheduled departure of the train. Article Title: Mumbai office boy earning Rs 3,500 a month faces Rs 1.46 crore tax assessment; alleges ex-employer misused KYC documents to obtain second PAN, ITAT quashes demand over invalid service of notice
Article Text:
In its September 21, 2026, order, the tribunal ruled that the department had failed to establish valid service of notice. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why ITAT ruled in favour of the ex-office boy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A man who says he worked as an office boy for Rs 3,500 a month found himself facing an income-tax assessment of nearly Rs 1.47 crore after the tax department linked him to a pharmaceutical business and transactions recorded in its bank account. His defence was that he had never run the business and that his former employer had allegedly misused his signatures and identity documents.The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, did not decide whether those allegations were true. Instead, it examined a more fundamental question: had the Income Tax Department validly served the notice that allowed it to reopen his assessment in the first place?In its September 21, 2026, order, the tribunal ruled that the department had failed to establish valid service and quashed the reassessment. The additions made in the proceedings consequently could not survive.The Income Tax Department initiated reassessment proceedings against a man after receiving information about transactions associated with a pharma company, described in the information available to the tax authorities as the man’s proprietary concern.The bank account records showed debit entries of Rs 1,27,62,500 and credit entries of Rs 18,85,000.The Assessing Officer treated the debit amount as unexplained expenditure under Section 69C of the Income Tax Act and the credit amount as unexplained income under Section 68. The assessment was completed under Sections 144 and 147, and the AO pegged the man’s total income at Rs 1,46,57,500.The assessee disputed the department's case on several fronts. According to his submissions, he had worked as an office boy for an employer from September 2009 for approximately 18 months, earning Rs 3,500 a month. He said he had provided signatures and KYC documents believing they were required for employment and security purposes.He alleged that the employer had used those documents to obtain another PAN without his knowledge. The man maintained that he had neither operated the pharma company nor undertaken the transactions in question. These remained his allegations; the tribunal did not establish that his former employer had misused his documents.The immediate legal dispute concerned a notice issued under Section 148 on March 27, 2019, which the man said he had never received.The tribunal examined the department's records and found that the notice sent to an address in Bandra East had remained unserved. The department subsequently relied on affixture, or pasting the notice on a premises in Bhiwandi.The problem was that the department had not established any connection between the man and the locked room where the notice was pasted. Its own records indicated that he did not reside at the Bhiwandi address.The tribunal observed: “Affixture on the door of any locked room, without establishing that it was the residence or business premises of the assessee, cannot constitute service upon him merely because a departmental officer had gone there and pasted a notice.”The department eventually obtained the man’s Vile Parle address and email details through enquiries from TransUnion CIBIL. A show-cause notice sent on November 22, 2019, reached him, and he responded five days later, disputing the PAN and denying knowledge of the company.The tribunal noted: “The final show-cause notice dated 22.11.2019 was thus the first communication which, on the basis of the material before us, is shown to have actually reached the assessee.”The man had raised objections before the assessment was completed. The tribunal held that his subsequent cooperation could not retrospectively cure the failure to serve the original notice. It stated: “Participation after raising a timely objection cannot retrospectively convert affixture at an unrelated premises into valid service.”The judges concluded that valid service of the notice was essential for the department to assume jurisdiction over the reassessment. Their order stated: “The assessment order passed under section 144 read with section 147 is, therefore, invalid and is hereby quashed.”The additions of Rs 1,27,62,500 and Rs 18,85,000 consequently fell with the reassessment. The appeal was allowed.The tribunal expressly left undecided the alleged misuse of the man’s PAN, signatures and KYC documents, as well as the genuineness of the underlying transactions, because the reassessment was invalid on the jurisdictional ground.
Article Summary: The Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT), Mumbai, did not decide whether those allegations were true. Instead, it examined a more fundamental question: had the Income Tax Department validly served the notice that allowed it to reopen his assessment in the first place? In its September 21, 2026, order, the tribunal ruled that the department had failed to establish valid service.

We are seeing growth across baskets... If we are able to carry on the trajectory, we can move towards the landmark of $1 trillion (goods and services exports) this year," commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal said.During the first half, goods and services exports were estimated at $479 billion, with Agrawal saying that there is usually an acceleration during the second half. On the import front, crude prices resulted in the value of goods entering India jumping 54% to $22.8 billion, while electronics saw an increase of 50% to $14.2 billion in Oct.

Article Title: Profits of banks rise 20% on interest income, loan growth
Article Text:
Profits of banks rise 20% on interest income, loan growth

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Indian banks' net profit rose 20% year-on-year to Rs 1.2 lakh crore in Q2FY27, driven by higher interest income, loan growth and one-time gains of around Rs 10,000 crore at large public sector banks (PSBs). The growth was also aided by a weak base, with profits having risen just 4.2% in Q2FY26.According to a CareEdge Ratings report, net profit of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) remained above Rs 1 lakh crore for the fourth consecutive quarter. Net interest income (NII) grew 15.4% as bank credit expanded around 19%. However, higher bond yields during the quarter sharply reduced treasury income. Profit growth varied across bank groups. PSBs reported a 15.9% increase in net profit, while private sector banks (PVBs) recorded 25.1% growth. Both groups reported similar operating profit growth, with the difference largely explained by provisions. PSBs' provisions rose 9.2%, while those of private banks fell 25.1%, reflecting an easing of stress in microfinance and unsecured lending at other private banks. The latter's growth was also supported by a weak base as their profits declined 4% in Q2FY26."Core lending drove bank earnings this quarter. Operating profit grew 13-15% y-o-y in both bank groups, so provisions explain the gap in their profit growth. Other private banks are catching up as credit costs ease," said Vineet Jain, senior director at CareEdge Ratings. He said the return on assets gap between other private banks and large private banks had halved over the past year, while higher provisions ahead of the expected credit loss (ECL) rules could weigh on returns.The report, which analysed 30 banks comprising 14 PSBs and 16 private banks, said profit growth was likely to moderate in H2FY27. Treasury income could remain weak, while the one-time gains recorded in Q2 are unlikely to recur. The 10-year govt security yield rose to 7.4% by Oct 19, adding to the pressure on treasury earnings.Provisions could also increase as banks build buffers ahead of the transition to ECL-based provisioning from April 1, 2027.
Article Summary: Net profit of scheduled commercial banks (SCBs) remained above Rs 1 lakh crore for the fourth consecutive quarter. Net interest income (NII) grew 15.4% as bank credit expanded around 19%. However, higher bond yields during the quarter sharply reduced treasury income.

Article Title: Oil supply to overtake demand in Dec quarter: IEA
Article Text:
Oil supply to overtake demand in Dec qtr: IEA

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Global oil supply is set to exceed demand in the Dec quarter for the first time since the US-Iran war began, with recovering exports from West Asia easing the supply crunch even as attacks on shipping continue, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday. A surplus supply also augurs well for prices with analysts suggesting that they will cool down, provided there are no fresh flareups in the region.The agency expects global oil supply to average around 105 million barrels per day (mbd) in the Dec quarter, 1.7 mbd higher than demand. This marks a sharp turnaround from its earlier forecast of a supply deficit.The recovery in supplies has eased pressure on crude prices. Brent Dated crude fell 32% from a peak of $136 per barrel in early Oct to around $93 per barrel, although it remained $22 per barrel above pre-war levels, IEA said. On Friday, Brent was trading at $95 a barrel, while the cost for Indian refiners on Thursday was estimated at $91.15.The increase in global oil supplies should have a moderating effect on prices, but replenishment of strategic reserves by countries that drew heavily from them during the conflict could push demand up, said Prashant Vasisht, senior vice-president at ICRA.Damaged oil infrastructure may also take time to recover, while continued geopolitical uncertainty could keep a premium on crude prices, he added."If the situation remains the same, prices may cool down to $75-80 per barrel, but they may not return to pre-war levels of $65-70 per barrel any time soon," he said.The improvement in supplies comes as West Asian producers step up exports despite disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. Gulf oil exports, excluding Oman, rose to 18.4 mbd in Oct, recovering to 74% of pre-war levels.Global oil supply rose by 2.3 mbd to 105.4 mbd in Oct, following an increase of 3 mbd in Sept. IEA expects supply to decline by an average 4.8 mbd in 2026 before rebounding by 6.6 mbd in 2027, led by a recovery in Gulf production.Global oil inventories rose by 52 million barrels in Oct, the first increase since June. Much of the build-up was in oil in transit, with volumes on water increasing by 86 million barrels, while on-land inventories continued to decline.On the demand side, IEA expects global oil consumption to decline by 2.7 mbd to 102.3 mbd in 2026 before recovering by 2 mbd in 2027.
Article Summary: Global oil supply is set to exceed demand in the Dec quarter for the first time since the US-Iran war began. Recovering exports from West Asia easing the supply crunch even as attacks on shipping continue. A surplus supply also augurs well for prices with analysts suggesting that they will cool down.

Article Title: Khambata 'strategised' to oust Srinivasan, say Tata Trusts VCs
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Two senior Tata Trusts trustees have accused a former colleague of helping the present leadership of the Trusts to reinforce control at the expense of his own fiduciary duties and the sanctity of the Tata model of governance.In a letter dated Nov 11, vice-chairmen of the Trusts, Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh , said Darius Khambata's account of the dispute between Noel Tata and a section of trustees was "incomplete in several material respects."They alleged that Khambata "strategised" to temporarily oust Srinivasan as a Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) trustee so that two new trustees could be inducted in Nov 2025. "There was nothing consensual about that process," they wrote.Their reply targets Khambata's Nov 2 letter, which described a Tata Sons listing as "existential" for the Trusts and said the company's engagement with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had been neither meaningful nor successful. Srinivasan and Singh said the record showed otherwise.Tata Sons began talking to the RBI in 2023, repaid its debt and applied for deregistration in March 2024, they said. The engagement continued after that."The trustees were kept informed throughout, and neither you nor any other trustee described the effort as inadequate at the time," they wrote.The RBI ruled after a two-year review that Tata Sons remained a systemically significant institution bound by the listing framework. The outcome, they said, reflected the regulator's judgment and "cannot be attributed to any deficiency in advocacy." "If, by 'meaningful' advocacy, you mean advocacy that secures preferential treatment or circumvents the applicable rules, then that would not be consistent with the Tata model you seek to uphold. "The letter rejected Khambata's claim that listing would threaten the Tata model. "We have seen no evidence for that proposition," the vice-chairmen said. They pointed to Novo Nordisk, Hershey, Lundbeck and Demant - each listed, each controlled or anchored by a foundation or trust. "An institution's character is preserved by the quality of its governance and accountability, not by its listing status."Khambata, a senior advocate, did not seek reappointment as a trustee when his term ended on Nov 8.Closer to home, they cited TCS, Tata Steel, Tata Power and Tata Motors, all listed and all of which have made long-gestation investments. "Disclosure and accountability bring discipline to how capital is allocated; they do not limit vision." The Trusts would stay shareholders of Tata Sons after a listing, and their "shareholding, dividends and the philanthropy those dividends fund would be unaffected".They asked whether Khambata's real concern was the Tata model or control of Tata Sons by the Trusts' present leadership. Where control becomes "an end in itself", they said, questions arise about trustees' fiduciary duties and the Trusts' continued entitlement to tax exemption. A listing of Tata Sons would end Trusts' superior voting rights on the company's board, which is why Trusts chairman Noel Tata is opposed to an IPO.The letter said the trustees of Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) unanimously recommended Chandrasekaran for a third term as executive chairman on July 28, 2025. Khambata supported that resolution and drafted it, they said. Two new trustees were inducted into SDTT on Nov 11, 2025, materially altering its balance, and Khambata proposed one of them, they said. In Feb 2026 Chandrasekran's reappointment was deferred, and no Trusts resolution reversed the July 28, 2025 decision.Khambata in his Nov 2 letter had called that resolution "overtaken" by events in Aug and Sept 2026. Srinivasan and Singh disagreed. "A unanimous resolution of trustees is not overtaken merely because honouring it later became difficult."They quoted a July 10, 2025 note from Khambata to Chandrasekaran, in which he called the group's results and plans "even more impressive than I'd imagined". Eighteen days later he backed the reappointment. "We would like to know what changed between that letter and the position you now take?" they asked.A trustee who praised the chairman in those terms, they added, and then "stood by passively while his reappointment was left in doubt for seven months, owes the Trusts and the public an explanation".Chandrasekaran concluded that the dignity of his office was being compromised by the delay and decided not to offer himself for reappointment, they said. The nomination and remuneration committee of Tata Sons unanimously asked him to reconsider. The company's board acted on Sept 17, they said, to end an uncertainty it had not created. On Sept 17, the Tata Sons board reappointed Chandrasekaran as chairman for a third term. Srinivasan supported the decision, while Noel opposed it.The Trusts, they said, were "more divided today than at any point in living memory". Khambata had argued, citing the Supreme Court's judgment in Tata Group v Cyrus Mistry, that a Trust nominee director must protect the Trusts' interests and that "there cannot be two classes of trustees".Srinivasan and Singh disputed that reading. "It did not extinguish a director's fiduciary duty to the company," they said, "nor turn a Trust nominee into a delegate bound to vote the Trusts' line. "On the Sept 11, 2025 vote not to renew Singh's tenure as a Tata Sons director, they said Khambata's own account showed a board seat decided by the need to secure a voting outcome rather than by the nominee's merit. They called that "difficult to reconcile" with the principles in his Nov 2 letter. "What you describe as betrayal is, in substance, a difference of view."No amount of spin-doctoring could mask what had happened, Srinivasan and Singh said, and that "applies to all concerned".
Article Summary: Two senior Tata Trusts trustees have accused a former colleague of helping the present leadership of the Trusts to reinforce control. Darius Khambata's account of the dispute between Noel Tata and a section of trustees was "incomplete in several material respects," they said.

BENGALURU: Newly listed Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses’ losses widened 43% year-on-year to Rs 88 crore in the September quarter, from Rs 61.6 crore a year earlier, due to higher employee stock-option expenses and finance costs.Total income grew 18% to Rs 4,652.7 crore from Rs 3,936.5 crore. That quarter included a Rs 639 crore provision covering doubtful dues, other assets and expected project losses in the infrastructure business.Zetwerk’s manufacturing order book rose 67% year on year to a record Rs 14,595 crore. The company said the order book typically converts into revenue over about two years.“Our manufacturing order book is at an all-time high of Rs 14,595 cr, and repeat customers contributed 83% of first-half revenue,” said cofounder and CEO Amrit Acharya.Manufacturing revenue rose 15% to Rs 2,546 crore in the quarter. Its own factories accounted for 60% of manufacturing revenue in the first half, up from 36% a year earlier. International customers contributed 41% of first-half manufacturing revenue, against 36% last year.The company said a greater share of in-house production, international customers and higher-margin products helped improve margins.Zetwerk supplies industrial and consumer products through its own factories and outside suppliers. Drawing upon almost 3 decades of work in national development, Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka developed YASHA, her five-pillar framework for Viksit Bharat 2047. In this edition of the Knowledge Series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, speaks with Aruna Lohia Goenka about- the power of skills to transform lives.Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 2026 Diwali visit to Bastar in Chhattisgarh must have stirred some memories. Wasn't that where your journey into skilling began, under rather unusual circumstances?Indeed, Sanjiv! The Bastar of the 1990s was very different from the Bastar we see today. It was a region deeply affected by Maoist violence, where opportunities for tribal communities were severely limited. We began opening schools and introducing what we then called- today's more fashionable term beingAnd do you know what struck me, Sanjiv? I seem to have inherited a rather unusual family addiction! My father had an addiction to opening schools, sometimes so quietly and anonymously that we discovered some of them only after his passing. My brothers, meanwhile, seem to have developed an addiction to creating employment opportunities wherever they go!The industrial enterprise my father and brothers built now has a presence in some 40 countries, principally in manufacturing and materials. But the family's interests occasionally take rather unexpected turns - organic farming in Tuscany, cotton cultivation in Uzbekistan! Different geographies, different pursuits, but one common thread: generating employment is in our DNA!And there is another connection I find rather charming. My father and my brother established schools in the jungles of Indonesia back in the 1970s. Decades later, there I was, opening schools and working with tribal communities in Bastar and other parts of India!(Laughs) I suppose addictions run in families. Fortunately, ours seem to be socially productive!Perhaps that is the thread connecting it all. Whether it is an industrial enterprise, a farm in Tuscany or a school deep in the forests of Bastar, the setting changes, but the underlying aspiration remains remarkably similar - to create opportunities for people to learn, work and build lives of dignity.And seeing Bastar's transformation today gives me enormous satisfaction.When you open a school in a place like Bastar, you are not merely opening a school. You are opening a future.Bastar was challenging enough. But surely you didn't stop there?(Laughs) Apparently, I have a weakness for difficult-to-reach places!From the forests of Bastar, my journey took me to the mountains of Himachal Pradesh, particularly Chamba, historically one of India's more backward districts and now part of NITI Aayog’s Aspirational Districts Programme. We established 50 skilling centres across Chamba district, bringing opportunities closer to communities that had long been underserved.You see, Sanjiv, talent is remarkably democratic. Opportunity, unfortunately, is not! A child's postal address should never determine the limits of their future.That is where Hunar becomes such a powerful equaliser.From remote villages to the corridors of power! How did you end up training the Delhi Police?That was an unexpected invitation! Former Delhi Police Commissioner B. K. Gupta asked whether we could help strengthen spoken English and soft skills within the police force. We mobilised resources through Teach India and began training Delhi Police personnel. I remain grateful to Commissioner B. K. Gupta for placing his trust in us. He was so pleased with the initiative that he extended an invitation to work in Tihar Jail, where he had earlier served as its chief before becoming Delhi Police Commissioner. There, we could help inmates, particularly those approaching release, acquire the skills and confidence to prepare for life beyond prison walls.And then, somehow, you landed in Tihar Jail! Should I be concerned!?!(Laughs) You are not the first to ask! There were occasions when friends would call my home and be told, quite casually, "She's gone to Tihar Jail." The silence at the other end was sometimes rather long! I suspect a few were already contemplating whether to arrange a lawyer!But jokes apart, Tihar remains one of the most satisfying places in which I have worked. Many inmates approaching release face an enormous challenge. Society may have served them a sentence, but it is often reluctant to offer them a second chance. Through skilling, communication and confidence-building, we prepared them for that second chance. A prison sentence may take away someone's freedom for a time. It should never take away their hope.And Sanjiv, sometimes the most important skill we can teach someone is the confidence to begin again.(Laughs) Fortunately, Tihar wasn't your only classroom in Delhi! What else were you experimenting with?Ashok Kumar Nigam, the then Commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), heard about our skilling initiatives and, inspired by the work we were already doing in other parts of Delhi, generously gave us access to, and space within, MCD schools, including those in the Defence Colony area, to introduce vocational skills such as beauty services and stitching. I remember how important it was to give young people skills they could actually use. Acquiring a skill gives a person immense confidence, a sense of self-worth and dignity. In other words, the ability to create one's own universe!And Sanjiv, never underestimate a skill simply because it does not come with a fancy designation!Your views about India's demographic dividend?Absolutely, Sanjiv! A demographic dividend is an opportunity, not an entitlement! Millions of young people are an enormous advantage - provided they have the skills, else our demographic dividend risks becoming a demographic bulge. That is why, in employability programmes such as Teach India, with which I am associated, we set a high bar: a minimum of 65% of our learners must secure gainful employment after completing their skilling programme. We measure success by livelihoods, not merely certificates!And remember, a skill should open a door, not become a ceiling.Finally, how doesfit into your vision of Viksit Bharat 2047?Sanjiv, for me, Hunar is the bridge between human potential and human dignity. Be it tribal communities in Bastar, or youth in the Chamba hills, or students in government schools or personnel in Delhi police, or inmates in Tihar Jail, I see one common aspiration: People want to learn. They want to earn. They want to contribute. And above all, they want to live with dignity.We often say India has 1.4 billion people. I see 1.4 billion possibilities! Our task is to turn those possibilities into capabilities, those capabilities into livelihoods, and those livelihoods into a more prosperous, inclusive and confident Bharat.That is the Hunar I believe in. And that is the India I dream of!
Article Summary: Impact Catalyst Aruna Lohia Goenka developed YASHA, her five-pillar framework for Viksit Bharat 2047. In this edition of the Knowledge Series, Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, speaks with Aruna.
